proposals.question: When can Thomas Haas be used, which rival may its owner inspect, what swap is permitted, and in what orientation do the two rivals remain? What must be announced, and is Thomas exhausted or discarded to use this ability?
proposals.expected_answer: At the end of the owner’s turn, optionally use Thomas once: look at the rival partly under the board, then optionally swap your own rival with that card. Both remain facedown. Openly announce whether you swapped. No exhaust or discard cost is printed.
proposals.novelty: Unique rival inspection and replacement procedure can change victory identity. Q17 asks only announcement; normal asset swap Q42 swaps assets, not rivals. This is not a fixed-value lookup.

proposals.question: An owned asset is already exhausted when its trigger occurs again before its owner’s next Refresh. Can the owner pay its exhaust cost again? How is exhaustion represented, and when and how does it ready normally?
proposals.expected_answer: No: an exhausted asset cannot be exhausted again. Rotate 90 degrees clockwise to exhaust. At the start of its owner’s Refresh step, ready it by rotating 90 degrees counterclockwise; trading or stealing it does not ready it.
proposals.novelty: Distinct repeated-trigger availability gate. Q14 explicitly treats cannot exhaust again as background, and other questions only ask printed exhaust costs. Repeated-trigger legality is not tested by knowing those costs.

proposals.question: May a counteroffer be another copy of the action proposed as the main offer or of an earlier counteroffer? Does having the same name make it illegal?
proposals.expected_answer: Yes, either duplicate is legal; RR15.7 expressly permits another copy. Normal proposal order and extra discard cost still apply.
proposals.novelty: Explicit offer-eligibility rule: rejects an unprinted uniqueness restriction. This is one question about duplicate legality, not one question for each duplicate physical card or renamed cost scenario.

proposals.question: How do you identify a district’s tier on the board, and does being in a higher tier inherently change its production or threat?
proposals.expected_answer: Count the colored bars under its name; this is its tier. District borders also share the color for their tier. Tiers have no inherent effect: printed cards can refer to them, including threat conditions; resource production uses the district’s printed resources and applicable modifiers.
proposals.novelty: Board interpretation required to apply tier-based card instructions. Existing event questions supply the relevant tier as a given; primary-icon identification Q80 does not ask tier identification.

proposals.question: At the start of Support, Isabel McGuire’s owner puts a deck card beside the counteroffer. Is the owner treated as supporting that offer, may an eligible owner then support the main offer normally, and does Locust Company’s restriction on that owner block Isabel’s deck card? What cost activates Isabel, and from which card source may its owner contribute to which offers?
proposals.expected_answer: At start of Support, optionally exhaust Isabel to place one top card of any action deck in support of either offer. This is not player support for eligibility purposes; an eligible owner may support either offer normally. Locust bars hand support for counteroffer, not Isabel’s deck card.
source_refs: FAQ Isabel McGuire and Locust Company
proposals.novelty: Makes currently unasked exhaust cost and deck/offer choice procedure explicitly tested; existing Q33 still tests its three meaningful eligibility branches.

proposals.question: Whose deal victory pays Coach Walden? When may Monica Singh steal, and who is the target? When Saul Eustecio is used, which player wins the deal and who gains capital in what order? Which of these effects requires exhausting its asset?
proposals.expected_answer: Coach: gain one when right neighbor wins, without exhaust cost. Monica: optionally steal two from countering player when owner loses as active, without exhaust cost. Saul: when countering player wins, optionally exhaust Saul; user gains one, then active gains one.
proposals.novelty: Explicitly tests the consequential limited-use cost difference rather than requiring that unasked key detail implicitly.

proposals.change: Qualify rival secrecy as during play; add that all players reveal rival cards when game ends.
proposals.expected_answer: Rival cards cannot be revealed or discussed during play. At either game ending, all players reveal them. Thomas publicly announces whether a swap occurred while the rival identities remain facedown.
proposals.reason: Current unqualified secrecy sentence omits explicit game-end revelation. Frozen original20 entries must remain history; do not silently edit.
